description: Maintenance status — the answer to "what maintenance is due?" (overdue / this month / next quarter). Without arguments: the organization overview — counts (overdue, dueSoon, blocked), the per-plan cards in `plans` (name, assignee, matchedCount / overdueCount / dueSoonCount / openTicketCount), the due list for the next ~90 days sorted soonest-first (each row names its plan, its item and, when a run ticket already exists, its ticketId) and the blocked rows needing attention. LEAD WITH THE PLANS: a maintenance plan is a real entity holding its checks together and it is the level a person acts on, so "Beamer-Wartung: 10 overdue, 2 due soon" is the answer — ten near-identical item rows are not. Keep the due list as the detail your user can ask for, and drop to a single check when they ask about one item. Every plan carries ONE default assignee (a person or a team), so all of its checks land on the same target by construction — that concentration is the design, never a finding to report. To hand someone a run ticket, look it up with list_tickets and give its title and `webUrl` link; the id itself is a machine handle, not something to read aloud. With itemId: that item's maintenance plans with last completed, next due and open ticket. Every date comes twice, epoch and ISO twin: `nextDueAtIso`, `openTicketDueAtIso` and the due list's `dueAtIso` are plain calendar days, `lastCompletedAtIso` is a UTC instant. Read the ISO one; this server does no timezone conversion, so never re-zone a calendar day. This is a REPORT: recording a check as done means walking its checklist, which happens in the app — plans themselves are created and edited there too, not through this connection.

itemId.description: Item id — returns that item's plan rows instead of the org overview

counts.description: Org-wide overdue / dueSoon / blocked counts — overview mode

due.description: Checks due within 90 days (overdue first), each naming its plan, item and open ticketId, plus `dueAt` (epoch) and `dueAtIso` (the plain calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD" — read that one) — overview mode

needsAttention.description: Rows blocked from scheduling — overview mode

plans.description: Plan rows — plan CARDS in overview mode, this item's plans in itemId mode

blocked.description: Why the row cannot be scheduled

lastCompletedAtIso.description: When the last check was recorded, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — read THIS one; the server does no timezone conversion

leadTimeDays.description: How early the run ticket opens

nextDueAtIso.description: When the next check is due, as a plain calendar day "YYYY-MM-DD" — a DAY, not a moment; do not re-zone it

openTicketDueAtIso.description: The run ticket's due date as a plain calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD"

openTicketId.description: The open run ticket. A machine handle: look it up with list_tickets and give your user its title and link, not this id. The check itself is recorded in the app
